errorCodes.meaning: No criterion the community publishes, or still honours within its `requirementsGrace`, has the supplied `requirementsDigest`.
The criterion states no credential query a wallet can answer — it requires no credential, or only credentials in formats the community does not accept over OpenID4VP.
The community holds no OpenID4VP verifier identity for the requested `clientIdPrefix`, or, when none was requested, for any prefix.
No join request with the supplied `requestId` exists, or it does not belong to the proof signer. The same code for both.
The supplied `requestId` names the signer's own join request, but it has been decided or withdrawn and can take no more evidence.
The applicant already has as many open wallet sessions as the community allows. Retry once one has been answered or has expired.

DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.
DigestMultibase.title: DigestMultibase

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

clientId.description: The full OpenID4VP client identifier the community presents to the wallet, prefix included (`decentralized_identifier:did:webvh:…`, `x509_hash:…`). It is the audience the wallet's key-binding JWT will name.

dcqlQuery.description: The DCQL query (OpenID4VP 1.0 §6) the wallet will be asked to satisfy: the criterion's published query, unchanged. Opaque here; its members are DCQL's own and keep DCQL's snake_case names.

expiresAt.description: When the session closes if no wallet has answered it. Minutes, not hours.

sessionId.description: Opaque, unguessable identifier of the session, carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. The applicant reads the outcome with vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status under it.

walletUri.description: The OpenID4VP invocation URI for this session, carrying `client_id` and `request_uri`, to be rendered as a QR code or opened as a deep link. Its scheme is the community's choice for the wallet ecosystem it serves — `openid4vp://`, `swiyu-verify://`, `haip-vp://` and others.

schema.description: An applicant asks the community to open an OpenID4VP 1.0 presentation session for one of its join criteria, so that a wallet which cannot sign Trust Tasks can present credentials as evidence for the applicant's join. The applicant is the document proof's signer, not a payload member. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

clientIdPrefix.description: The OpenID4VP 1.0 client identifier prefix the community should identify itself to the wallet with — a DID (`decentralized_identifier`, as swiyu wallets expect) or an X.509 certificate (`x509_hash`, as EUDI wallets expect). Values are OpenID4VP's own and are carried verbatim. Absent: the community's default. A community holding no verifier identity of the requested kind refuses with `verifierNotConfigured`.

criterion.description: The `requirementsDigest` of the criterion the applicant is gathering evidence for, as vtc/join-requests/manifest (0.3 or later) published it — the same value vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 carries as its `criterion`. Naming the version, not only the criterion, fixes the DCQL query the wallet is asked to satisfy to the one the applicant read.

requestId.description: An existing join request of the applicant's to record the evidence on. Absent: the community holds the evidence, for a bounded period of its own policy, for the applicant's next vtc/join-requests/submit under the same criterion.
